title: EURETINA 2026: Global RETFound expands to 108 partners in effort to build a truly global foundation model
key_facts: At the 26th EURETINA Congress in Vienna, UCL research fellow and Moorfields consultant Paul Nderitu gave an update on Global RETFound, a retinal-image foundation model project.
The project now has 108 partners from more than 40 countries after a year of recruitment.
Three-quarters of partners shared generative models trained on local data for synthesising images; 27 sites shared real data.
The team plans to synthesise about 100 million colour fundus (back-of-eye) images and combine them with real data, hoped to be a 100-fold increase over the original RETFound.

More than 20 sites are trialling use cases from diabetic retinopathy and macular degeneration to retinopathy of prematurity; validation over coming months is the priority and the model is meant to be open access for research.
A peer-reviewed protocol paper was recently published; a second recruitment round is planned for 2027 to fill data gaps in regions such as Africa, South America and Central Asia.
quote_evidence: The project has spent the past year recruiting collaborators and now includes 108 partners from more than 40 countries, Nderitu said.
Nderitu emphasised that validation over the coming months is the priority, and the team aims to make the model open access for research.
"We want to see other global foundation models being made," he said.
why_it_matters_hint: A research effort to stop eye-disease AI from working only for the populations it was trained on, by pooling data from 40-plus countries.
event_date: EURETINA 2026 congress, Vienna; exact date not stated in the article (published 4 Oct 2026)
